<details>
The `flydigi-vader4d.install` script contains standard post-install, post-upgrade, and post-remove hooks commonly used in Arch Linux packages. The `post_install` function reloads and triggers udev rules to ensure the device driver rules are properly loaded, which is a typical operation for hardware support packages. It also prints a helpful message instructing the user to enable the associated systemd user service, which is expected behavior.

The `post_upgrade` function simply calls `post_install`, ensuring consistent setup after updates. The `post_remove` function disables and stops the user service, cleaning up the system state during removal. All operations are confined to standard system configuration and user service management, with no network activity, file manipulation outside expected scope, or execution of external payloads.

There is no obfuscated code, suspicious commands, or unexpected behavior. The use of `|| true` ensures the script continues even if udev commands fail, improving robustness. These practices are consistent with AUR packaging norms and support the stated purpose of enabling a gaming device driver.
</details>
